_about: Public-domain William Snodgrass (1827-1906), Scottish-born Presbyterian minister at Charlottetown and St Paul's, Montreal, and principal of Queen's College, Kingston, for the Word Hoard: his funeral and farewell sermons, The Good Centurion, The Two Builders, The Sacredness of Learning, and an address to the Charlottetown Young Men's Christian Association. Texts are from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 108 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

wsnodgrass-ymca-1856: An address delivered at the inauguration of the Charlottetown Young Men's Christian Association : on the evening of February 6, 1856 ([Charlottetown, P.E.I.? : s.n.], 1856)
wsnodgrass-sermon-1857: A Sermon, preached on the 1st March, 1857, being the first Sabbath after the funeral of Hew Ramsay, Esq (Montreal : Printed by John Lovell, 1857)

wsnodgrass-good-centurion: The good centurion, an example for Scotchmen in Canada (Montreal, Becket, 1862)
wsnodgrass-two-builders: The two builders, or, The conclusion of the matter ([Montreal? : s.n.], 1863)
wsnodgrass-sacredness-learning: The sacredness of learning; address delivered at the opening of session 1864-65, Queen's college (Kingston, [s.n.], 1864)
wsnodgrass-ministers-farewell: A minister's farewell (Montreal, Printed by J. Lovell, 1864)
